steps.text: Hooke's law: extension is proportional to force, F = kx, but only up to the elastic limit.
Beyond the limit of proportionality the graph curves; beyond the elastic limit the material is permanently deformed.
Stress = F/A and strain = x/L; Young modulus E = stress/strain.
Elastic energy stored = area under the force–extension graph = ½kx².
Work is done stretching a material; it is recovered fully only if the deformation is elastic.
The gradient of the force–extension graph is the spring constant k.
